12.0.0.en: The impurity of her infirmity: the days of a woman's monthly period.

12.0.1.en: Bearing children was a blessing and a divine command before the Fall. But after the Fall and the curse, bearing offspring became the bearing of sinful children who carry the sin of Adam and Eve. So childbirth was counted as an uncleanness, so that the woman might remember her sins and so that it might be an occasion for repentance. And because whatever she touches would be unclean, this calls her to complete rest, which helps her regain her health after the labors of childbirth. The woman who gives birth is unclean for seven days if she bears a male child.

12.1.0.en: Foreskin: a small piece of skin that is removed from the child's male organ.

12.1.1.en: The newborn is circumcised on the eighth day so that he may become a member of the people of God. His nature is renewed on the eighth day, which signifies eternity, where he receives a spiritual nature fit for the Kingdom. And because circumcision is a type of Baptism, which gives us new life in Christ and prepares us for the Kingdom of Heaven, it is no longer necessary to perform it in the New Testament, and when Christians do it, it is for health reasons only.

12.2.0.en: The sanctuary: the tabernacle of meeting.

12.2.1.en: The blood of her purifying: the blood that comes after childbirth. Blood is the basis of life, and its flowing points to the death that came upon man because of sin. So in the Old Testament it was considered an uncleanness and required a period of purification; but in the New Testament, through the death of Christ and the shedding of His blood, we receive cleansing from our sins, and the flow of blood is not considered an uncleanness. The woman remained in her uncleanness for the following thirty-three days, so that the whole period was forty days from the birth. She was not to touch anything holy or come to the house of the Lord. In the New Testament, Christ has lifted uncleanness from woman and from all His people by His salvation; yet she cannot partake of the Holy Mysteries, because of the lack of fitness and bodily cleanliness. The Law set forty days so that the effects of the flow of blood would end for all women, even those who take longer than others.

12.3.0.en: The period is doubled in the case of the birth of a female child, so that the mother may remember that the woman fell into sin before the man, tempted him, and afterward caused him to fall into sin. So the mother offers a doubled repentance for herself, not for the baby girl, so that she may live with God in depth and encourage her husband to the spiritual life.

12.3.1.en: Celebrate the feast of your Baptism at every baptism you attend, just as you celebrate your birthday, because Baptism is the beginning of your spiritual life, your sonship to God, and your worthiness to inherit eternal life. Remember that you have received a new nature, so that you may live to God in all your thoughts, words and deeds, and not to the world.

12.4.0.en: A lamb of the first year: one year old.

12.4.1.en: A young pigeon: a small dove.

12.4.2.en: We notice that the sacrifice is one and the same for the newborn, male or female, a sign of the equality of the two sexes in God's sight (Gal 3:28, Col 3:11). And the pairing of the burnt offering and the sin offering, which are the lamb and the young pigeon, shows the double work of Christ in:

12.4.4.en: 2- Paying the price of the sins of humanity (the sin offering).

12.5.0.en: The fountain of her blood: the blood that was flowing from the woman who had given birth.

12.5.1.en: Offering the burnt offering and the sin offering for the woman who has given birth cleanses her from the blood that was flowing from her after childbirth, and this is a type of the blood of Christ, which cleanses us in the sacraments of Baptism, confession and Communion. The blood that a woman sheds is a symbol of the death that came upon the human race because of sin. Death was considered an uncleanness, and whoever touched the dead became unclean; likewise blood was considered an uncleanness. But Christ by His blood took away our sins, so that the blood a woman sheds in the New Testament is not considered an uncleanness but a health ailment.

12.6.0.en: The poor could substitute a young dove or a young turtledove for the lamb of the burnt offering. This was the sacrifice of the Virgin Mary, who fulfilled the rite in spite of the purity of her childbirth, so that her humility and her fulfilling of the Law might be clear to us. The Virgin was a human being upon whom lay the sin of Adam and Eve, and she was not conceived without stain, so she needed purification through the sacrifices that signify the sacrifice of Christ her Savior. We notice that the sin offering is a turtledove or a young pigeon, a cheap bird, to take away the sin of the woman who has given birth; but the burnt offering is according to the financial means of the woman giving birth: either a lamb, or a turtledove, or a young pigeon.

12.6.1.en: Let us remember Him who became poor for our sake, though He is the source of all riches, so that we may thank Him abundantly, and so that all the material things of the world and their wealth may become small in our eyes. Then we shall not grow weary from material hardship, or bodily weakness, or any problems that pass over us, because our God is strong, and our Redeemer will deliver us from them all and comfort our hearts during these afflictions.

12.6.2.en: Leprosy of persons and of garments: introduction

12.6.3.en: Leprosy is a contagious skin disease that disfigures the body; it existed in the Old Testament.

12.6.4.en: Leprosy was connected with sin and might be a punishment for it, as in the case of Miriam the sister of Moses (Num 12:10-15), Gehazi the disciple of the prophet Elisha (2 Kgs 5:27), and King Uzziah (2 Chr 26:19-23). The priest would diagnose the disease and then confirm that it had gone, after the sick person had been separated for a period of time from mixing with the people. When he was healed of the disease, he offered sacrifices through the priest, and God forgave him his sins.

12.6.5.en: There was no cure for this disease, but healing comes from God. The healing is called cleansing, because it is deliverance from the effects of sin.

12.6.6.en: (a) Leprosy of persons (vv. 1-46). It includes various symptoms that reveal the presence of the disease, which are:

12.6.7.en: (1) White hair (vv. 1-3). 1 And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, saying, 2 “When a man shall have in the skin of his flesh a rising, a scab, or bright spot, and it be in the skin of his flesh like the plague of leprosy; then he shall be brought unto Aaron the priest, or unto one of his sons the priests: 3 And the priest shall look on the plague in the skin of the flesh: and when the hair in the plague is turned white, and the plague in sight be deeper than the skin of his flesh, it is a plague of leprosy: and the priest shall look on him, and pronounce him unclean.”

13.0.0.en: The Lord spoke to Moses because he was the leader of the people, and to Aaron because he was the high priest, responsible with his sons for carrying out the Law.

13.1.0.en: A rising: a swelling, a tumor, or the mark of a wound.

13.1.2.en: A bright spot: a patch on the skin of a different color.

13.1.3.en: If a raised part, or a red or shining white part, was noticed on the skin of any Jewish person, they would bring him to the priest so that he might examine it and know whether these were signs of leprosy or of another skin disease.

13.1.4.en: The examination was held between the sixth hour and the ninth hour by Jewish reckoning, that is, from twelve to three in the afternoon, when the light of the sun is strong. The sick person's coming to the priest is a symbol of the sinner's turning to the father of confession to repent, so that the priest may examine his sins and guide him to the means of curing sin. The examination was not made on the Sabbath, because it is a day set apart for worship, so it was put off to the following day; and if the priest wished, he could seek the help of some experienced persons from among the people to diagnose the disease.

13.2.0.en: The priest examines him. If he finds in the discolored skin hair that has turned white, and also a depression in the skin, he is sure that it is the disease of leprosy, and he orders that the person be declared unclean and isolated.

13.2.1.en: If strange thoughts war against you and you doubt yourself, then turn to your father of confession and disclose your thoughts to him, and God will guide you through his tongue, so that you may resist the deceiving devil, repel the thoughts, and fortify yourself with the means of grace as your spiritual father guides you.

13.2.2.en: (2) The bright spot (vv. 4-8). 4 “If the bright spot be white in the skin of his flesh, and in sight be not deeper than the skin, and the hair thereof be not turned white; then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague seven days: 5 And the priest shall look on him the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague in his sight be at a stay, and the plague spread not in the skin; then the priest shall shut him up seven days more: 6 And the priest shall look on him again the seventh day: and, behold, if the plague be somewhat dark, and the plague spread not in the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean: it is but a scab: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean. 7 But if the scab spread much abroad in the skin, after that he hath been seen of the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen of the priest again: 8 And if the priest see that, behold, the scab spreadeth in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a leprosy.”

13.3.0.en: The second symptom that the disease of leprosy may have is the appearance of a white spot in the skin, but without white hair in it and without a depression in the skin. This symptom may be leprosy or a similar skin disease, so the priest shuts him up with him for seven days, to make sure first whether the disease advances and other symptoms appear. The confinement was in tents near the tabernacle of meeting in the wilderness of Sinai, or in side rooms of the Temple in Jerusalem. The elders of the Jews did not shut up a suspected person on his wedding day or during the feasts of Unleavened Bread and Tabernacles.

13.4.0.en: In his sight: as the priest sees it.

13.4.1.en: If after seven days the priest notices that the white spot has not increased, he shuts him up for another seven days to be sure.

13.5.1.en: Scab: a mark that is not harmful to the skin.

13.5.2.en: If after the second seven days the priest notices that the spot has not increased but its color has become darker, it is not leprosy; so he pronounces him clean, because this is merely a mark on the skin and not leprosy.

13.6.0.en: If after seven days the priest notices that the spots on the skin have increased, he shuts him up another seven days to make sure that it is the disease of leprosy.

13.7.0.en: If the priest notices that the spots on the skin have spread and increased, he judges that it is the disease of leprosy and orders the sick person to be isolated because of his uncleanness.

13.7.1.en: Do not be hasty in your judgments, lest you wrong another. Ask for God's guidance, think calmly, and seek counsel from the spiritual fathers as much as you can, especially in big decisions, and be confident that God will value your prayer and your turning to Him and will guide you to what is for your good and the good of others.

13.7.2.en: (3) White spots with raw flesh in them (vv. 9-11). 9 “When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest; 10 And the priest shall see him: and, behold, if the rising be white in the skin, and it have turned the hair white, and there be quick raw flesh in the rising; 11 It is an old leprosy in the skin of his flesh, and the priest shall pronounce him unclean, and shall not shut him up: for he is unclean.”

13.7.3.en: The third case of leprosy is the presence of white spots higher than the ordinary skin, that is, a swelling, with white hair in it, but inside these white spots there are portions of living flesh, that is, the natural color of the body's flesh. In this case the priest judges that it is the disease of leprosy and isolates the sick person because of his uncleanness. This symptom declares that the disease of leprosy is of long standing in the sick person, that is, chronic, and so he is certainly unclean.

13.7.4.en: Do not be lenient with sin until it becomes deep in you and you grow accustomed to it, and you need greater striving to be rid of it. Cut off the sources of sin from the beginning and confess it, and you will be cleansed of it quickly with little striving.

13.8.0.en: The fourth case in the appearance of the disease of leprosy is the spreading of the white spots until they cover the whole body, that is, the whole skin becomes white. This means that the course of the disease is complete and the skin will return to its natural color, so the priest pronounces him clean. Spiritually, this signifies that the sick person has felt his complete lack, repented and humbled himself, and so deserves forgiveness and healing.

13.9.0.en: If the leprosy spreads and covers the whole body, but the priest discovers the presence of even small portions of living flesh, that is, the natural color of the body, among the white, he judges him leprous and unclean. Spiritually, this signifies wavering between a life of purity and uncleanness, or between good and evil.

13.10.0.en: In the last case mentioned in (vv. 14, 15), if the portions that were the color of living flesh change and become white, that is, the whole body becomes white, it is like the case mentioned in (vv. 12, 13), and he is pronounced clean.

13.10.1.en: Try to remain steadfast in your spiritual path and in carrying out your rule of prayer, so that you may abide in life with God and receive forgiveness, for the wavering person is unclean before God.

13.11.0.en: The case here arose as a mark in the skin after an abscess or boil that left a white sign tending to redness, or a raised mark, so he is brought to the priest.

13.12.0.en: The priest examines the sick person. If he finds in the mark of the boil a depression in the skin with white hair in it, he knows that it is the disease of leprosy and pronounces him unclean; that is, he finds in the place of the boil some parts raised in the skin and other parts depressed.

13.13.0.en: If by examination the priest finds that the place of the boil is a dark-colored spot, with no depression in the skin or white hair, he shuts him up seven days to be sure whether it is the disease of leprosy or not, because these signs are not sufficient to diagnose leprosy.

13.14.0.en: If the priest notices that the spot spreads in the skin, it is the disease of leprosy, and he pronounces the sick person unclean.

13.15.0.en: If the spot that is in the mark of the boil does not spread, it is merely a mark of it and not one of the symptoms of leprosy, so the priest pronounces him clean.

13.15.1.en: If you have repented of a sin, do not keep traces of it in your life, such as an evil friend, bad pictures, or any matters that had a connection with sin. Rather, get rid of all of it firmly, lest it bring you back to worse sins.

13.15.2.en: Keep away from the sources of sin and cling to the Church, and you will be steadfast in the life of repentance.

13.15.3.en: (6) A burning of fire (vv. 24-28). 24 “Or if there be any flesh, in the skin whereof there is a hot burning, and the quick flesh that burneth have a white bright spot, somewhat reddish, or white; 25 Then the priest shall look upon it: and, behold, if the hair in the bright spot be turned white, and it be in sight deeper than the skin; it is a leprosy broken out of the burning: wherefore the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy. 26 But if the priest look on it, and, behold, there be no white hair in the bright spot, and it be no lower than the other skin, but be somewhat dark; then the priest shall shut him up seven days: 27 And the priest shall look upon him the seventh day: and if it be spread much abroad in the skin, then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is the plague of leprosy. 28 And if the bright spot stay in his place, and spread not in the skin, but it be somewhat dark; it is a rising of the burning, and the priest shall pronounce him clean: for it is an inflammation of the burning.”

13.16.0.en: "The quick flesh that burneth": the skin that has been renewed in the place of the burn.

13.16.1.en: Treatment by cauterizing was used anciently, but after the skin grows back in the place of the burn, its color may be white or white tending to redness.

13.17.0.en: This must be shown to the priest so that he may examine it for the three signs of leprosy explained above, which are:

13.17.1.en: a depression in the surface of the skin, whiteness of the hair, and spreading. If he finds them, he pronounces the sick person unclean.

13.18.0.en: There may remain only a mark of the burn of a color darker than the color of the skin, so the sick person is isolated for seven days so that the priest may be sure of his cleanness.

13.19.0.en: If the mark spreads, it was leprosy; but if it does not spread, it is merely a mark of the burn, which is harmless.

13.19.1.en: Pray much that God may remove the trace of the wars of lust from your heart, so that you do not desire your old sins lest you be burned by their fire once again. Resist evil thoughts by repeating prayers, however long the thoughts continue, and be confident that God rejoices in this striving of yours, for it is evidence of your repentance, and He upholds you until you are rid of them and come out of this war with a stronger spiritual will and spiritual growth.

13.19.2.en: (7) A plague on the head or beard (vv. 29-37). 29 “If a man or woman have a plague upon the head or the beard; 30 Then the priest shall see the plague: and, behold, if it be in sight deeper than the skin; and there be in it a yellow thin hair; then the priest shall pronounce him unclean: it is a dry scall, even a leprosy upon the head or beard. 31 And if the priest look on the plague of the scall, and, behold, it be not in sight deeper than the skin, and that there is no black hair in it; then the priest shall shut up him that hath the plague of the scall seven days: 32 And in the seventh day the priest shall look on the plague: and, behold, if the scall spread not, and there be in it no yellow hair, and the scall be not in sight deeper than the skin; 33 He shall be shaven, but the scall shall he not shave; and the priest shall shut up him that hath the scall seven days more: 34 And in the seventh day the priest shall look on the scall: and, behold, if the scall be not spread in the skin, nor in sight deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean. 35 But if the scall spread much in the skin after his cleansing; 36 Then the priest shall look on him: and, behold, if the scall be spread in the skin, the priest shall not seek for yellow hair; he is unclean. 37 But if the scall be in his sight at a stay, and that there is black hair grown up therein; the scall is healed, he is clean: and the priest shall pronounce him clean.”

13.20.1.en: The skin disease may be in the head or beard of a man or a woman. As the Apostle Paul says that the head of the man is Christ, a plague in the head of a man signifies a weakness or defect that has afflicted his faith in Christ; but the head of the woman is the man, so a plague in the head of a woman signifies a defect in her relationship with her husband. As for the beard, it signifies dignity and honor, so a plague in it signifies the effect of sins in dishonoring a person's spiritual dignity.

13.21.1.en: Thin: fine (weak). Scall: a scalp disease (a contagious skin disease). If the priest notices a depression of the skin and the presence of yellow hair, he pronounces the sick person unclean, because it is the disease of leprosy, which has appeared in the form of a scall on the head or beard.

13.22.0.en: If the priest notices that the skin is not depressed but the hair is not black and its color has changed, this means that some of the signs have disappeared, so isolation for seven days is called for, to be deliberate in judgment, and the lack of spreading is a sign that calls for further confirmation.

13.23.0.en: The priest shaves the place around the plague so that it appears clearly, and shuts up the sick person, isolated, for another seven days. If it is established that it has not spread, he is clean, and he washes his clothes as a confirmation of his cleanness.

13.24.0.en: But if the spots spread in the skin and the priest notices this after shutting him up seven days, it means that it is leprosy, and he pronounces him unclean even if he finds no yellow hair.

13.25.0.en: The sick person is not counted clean unless the spreading of the disease has stopped and black hair, that is, strong and sound hair, has reappeared. This signifies the person's return to his spiritual strength, and so he is clean.

13.25.1.en: Keep up the means of grace to be rid of every weakness that befalls you because of sin, and regular Communion is among the most important of these strengthening means.

13.25.2.en: (8) The freckled spot (vv. 38, 39). 38 “If a man also or a woman have in the skin of their flesh bright spots, even white bright spots; 39 Then the priest shall look: and, behold, if the bright spots in the skin of their flesh be darkish white; it is a freckled spot that groweth in the skin; he is clean.”

13.26.0.en: Bright spots, bright spots: patches, patches.

13.26.1.en: Freckled spot: this is the disease of vitiligo, which appears in the form of white patches on the skin, and it is not contagious.

13.26.2.en: If the priest finds a person with dark white patches on his skin, that is, not pure white, and there are no other signs in the skin, this is not leprosy but the disease of vitiligo, so he pronounces him clean.

13.26.3.en: Do not be hasty in judging people, for they may have an appearance that you think is connected with sin .. Be patient in judgment, for they may be pure, and do not busy yourself much with judging others, but look only for virtues, make excuses for mistakes, and pray for everyone, and for yourself before them.

13.26.4.en: (9) Baldness (vv. 40-44). 40 “And the man whose hair is fallen off his head, he is bald; yet is he clean. 41 And he that hath his hair fallen off from the part of his head toward his face, he is forehead bald: yet is he clean. 42 And if there be in the bald head, or bald forehead, a white reddish sore; it is a leprosy sprung up in his bald head, or his bald forehead. 43 Then the priest shall look upon it: and, behold, if the rising of the sore be white reddish in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, as the leprosy appeareth in the skin of the flesh; 44 He is a leprous man, he is unclean: the priest shall pronounce him utterly unclean; his plague is in his head.”

13.27.0.en: Bald: the falling out of all the hair of the head.

13.27.1.en: Forehead bald: the falling out of the hair from the front of the head only.

13.27.2.en: The condition here is not a disease, whether through the falling out of all the hair of the head or the hair from the front of the head only.

13.28.0.en: But the appearance of the symptoms of leprosy in the head establishes the person's uncleanness, and they are white spots tending to redness.

13.28.1.en: Having any lack in you in material respects, such as poverty or sickness, is no disgrace to you, provided it is not accompanied by any symptoms of sin, that is, the lack does not lead to grumbling, or resentment of others, or any bad treatment. Accept your inability and your weakness, do not compare yourself with anyone, and be confident that God will make you complete, and you will be in fullness and spiritual happiness.

13.28.2.en: (10) The law of the leper (vv. 45, 46). 45 “And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and his head bare, and he shall put a covering upon his upper lip, and shall cry, Unclean, unclean. 46 All the days wherein the plague shall be in him he shall be defiled; he is unclean: he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his habitation be.”

13.29.0.en: The camp: the place where the people's tents were set up.

13.29.1.en: The leper is obliged to do five things once his infection with leprosy is established, which are:

13.29.2.en: 1- He rends his clothes, and this signifies the exposure of sin, since the body of the one afflicted with the disease is shown; note that this applied to men only and not to women, out of regard for their modesty.

13.29.3.en: 2- Baring the head, that is, not wearing a turban or the like, and this signifies his loss of dignity because of sin.

13.29.4.en: 3- The man covering his upper lip, as a symbol of his loss of his spiritual manliness because of his weakness and his fall into sin.

13.29.5.en: 4- He cries out about himself that he is unclean, and this means his confession of his sin, and also that no one may come near him and touch him and so make others unclean.

13.29.6.en: 5- He is isolated from the place where people dwell, as a symbol of his loss of his communion in the Church.

13.29.7.en: All these duties help the sick person to repent and reject all his old sins, so that God may have compassion on him and heal him of his disease. Leprosy is a disease that indicates the uncleanness of man, and it has symptoms as already explained in this chapter. God allows this disease because of man's falling into great sins, and there is no healing from this disease by drugs or any medical treatment; healing comes from God, confirming that this disease is connected with sin and its cure is repentance.

13.29.8.en: Take care to confess your sins and humble yourself before God, and do not be angry if your father of confession gives you a discipline such as deprivation from Communion, for all this helps you to repent, so that you receive God's mercies and regain your spiritual strength.

13.29.9.en: (b) Leprosy of garments (vv. 47-59). 47 “The garment also that the plague of leprosy is in, whether it be a woollen garment, or a linen garment; 48 Whether it be in the warp, or woof; of linen, or of woollen; whether in a skin, or in any thing made of skin; 49 And if the plague be greenish or reddish in the garment, or in the skin, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; it is a plague of leprosy, and shall be shewed unto the priest: 50 And the priest shall look upon the plague, and shut up it that hath the plague seven days: 51 And he shall look on the plague on the seventh day: if the plague be spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in a skin, or in any work that is made of skin; the plague is a fretting leprosy; it is unclean. 52 He shall therefore burn that garment, whether warp or woof, in woollen or in linen, or any thing of skin, wherein the plague is: for it is a fretting leprosy; it shall be burnt in the fire. 53 And if the priest shall look, and, behold, the plague be not spread in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; 54 Then the priest shall command that they wash the thing wherein the plague is, and he shall shut it up seven days more: 55 And the priest shall look on the plague, after that it is washed: and, behold, if the plague have not changed his colour, and the plague be not spread; it is unclean; thou shalt burn it in the fire; it is fret inward, whether it be bare within or without. 56 And if the priest look, and, behold, the plague be somewhat dark after the washing of it; then he shall rend it out of the garment, or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the woof: 57 And if it appear still in the garment, either in the warp, or in the woof, or in any thing of skin; it is a spreading plague: thou shalt burn that wherein the plague is with fire. 58 And the garment, either warp, or woof, or whatsoever thing of skin it be, which thou shalt wash, if the plague be departed from them, then it shall be washed the second time, and shall be clean. 59 This is the law of the plague of leprosy in a garment of woollen or linen, either in the warp, or woof, or any thing of skins, to pronounce it clean, or to pronounce it unclean.”

13.30.0.en: Garments too may be infected with leprosy. A person's clothes signify his conduct, so it must be pure in his appearance, his speech and his behavior.

13.31.0.en: Warp: the lengthwise threads of the fabric.

13.31.1.en: Woof: the crosswise threads of the fabric.

13.31.2.en: The spot carrying the infection may appear in the lengthwise or crosswise threads of the fabric of the garment, whether wool or linen, and it appears also in the garment or article of skin, and its color tends to greenish or reddish. Then the garment is shown to the priest.

13.32.0.en: The priest examines the garments. If he finds in them the symptoms mentioned above, he isolates them for seven days; and if the plague spreads, the garment is leprous and unclean.

13.33.0.en: The priest burns the garment because it is unclean and to prevent the spread of infection, and this signifies cutting off sin and keeping away from it completely, whatever the loss.

13.34.0.en: Any thing: that is, articles made of skin.

13.34.1.en: If the plague has not spread, the priest has it washed and isolates the garment for another week.

13.35.1.en: Bare: the worn place in the cloth.

13.35.2.en: If the plague has not spread but its appearance remains as it was and has not disappeared with washing, and this is clear after the garment has dried, the garment is considered unclean and must be burned. The infection will have caused a hole or erosion, whether on the inside of the garment or the outside. This signifies the need for continued repentance in order to cut off any traces of sin.

13.36.0.en: But if the color of the infection remains dark after washing, the priest tears out only the area of the plague, out of care not to spoil and lose the whole garment; but it is torn out lest it turn into leprosy afterward. This signifies being on guard against what leads to sin and keeping away from it.

13.37.0.en: Spreading: living leprosy that breeds and increases.

13.37.1.en: If the infection reappears in the garment, it is then of the living kind that can spread, so the whole garment is burned.

13.38.0.en: But if the plague disappears after washing, it was merely a spot, so the garment is washed again to confirm its cleanness and then used again because it is clean. Thus one must guard against every appearance of evil.

13.39.0.en: Such is the law concerning the leprosy of garments.

13.39.1.en: Would that you were careful about your conduct and appearance, and even about every word you utter and every word you hear, lest by hearing it repeatedly it makes you fall into sin. And do not forget that you will give an account on the Day of Judgment for every idle word. In this way you keep yourself pure from every evil and every appearance of evil.

13.39.2.en: The cleansing of the leper and leprosy of houses: introduction

13.39.3.en: To show the hideousness of sin so that man may hate it, the leper is isolated, because his disease signifies uncleanness, and he stays outside the camp, away from the people, until he repents, and then God heals him, since he has no medical cure. Then he needs three stages for his cleansing, so that he may feel the importance of the new, pure life that he will receive, hold fast to it and keep away from every sin. These steps of cleansing signify the redemption that Christ accomplished on the Cross and gave us in the Church and her sacraments.
